name: Three-Tier Serverless Web Application
description: Design a scalable, cost-efficient three-tier serverless web application on AWS with authentication, CDN, API management, serverless compute, and NoSQL storage.
user_problem: Design a secure, scalable three-tier web application on AWS with the following requirements: (1) A presentation tier with CDN for global content delivery, static asset hosting, and user authentication, (2) A business logic tier with serverless compute behind a managed API layer, (3) A data tier with a serverless NoSQL database for storing application data, (4) Proper security with user authentication and authorization, (5) Cost efficiency using pay-as-you-go serverless services, (6) Monitoring and logging for all tiers.

reference_architecture.full_text:
A three-tier architecture is a popular implementation of a multi-tier architecture and consists of a presentation tier, business logic tier, and data tier. A three-tier architecture separates an application's functionality into distinct layers to enable scalability, modularity, and flexibility in software development. This type of architecture is suitable for building a wide range of applications such as web applications, enterprise systems, and mobile apps. Cost efficiency is a prominent advantage of using AWS serverless services. These services decrease the need for provisioning and managing servers, reducing operational overhead and labor costs. Serverless services like AWS Lambda and Amazon API Gateway use a pay-as-you-go model, so you only pay for the resources you consume, providing significant savings compared to maintaining idle infrastructure. Serverless technologies also feature automatic scaling and built-in high availability to increase agility and optimize costs.

Presentation Tier: The presentation tier is where users interact with the application, such as a webpage or an app. Amazon S3 hosts static and dynamic assets, like a React Single Page Application (SPA), and distributes them to end users. S3 provides 5 GB of standard storage, 20,000 GET requests, and 2,000 PUT requests. Amazon CloudFront is used with Amazon S3 for a faster and more performant distribution of assets to end users. CloudFront gives access to the AWS content delivery network with more than 410 points of presence worldwide, including 1 TB of data transfer out to the internet per month and 10 million HTTP/HTTPS requests per month. Amazon Cognito user pools authenticate users and can be integrated within the application's UI for a seamless login experience. Amazon Cognito has an Always Free Tier, including up to 50,000 monthly active users, 10 GBs of cloud sync storage, and 1 million sync operations per month. AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall) can be attached to CloudFront to protect against common web exploits such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting (XSS). CloudFront also supports AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) for provisioning and managing SSL/TLS certificates for HTTPS connections, ensuring encryption in transit.

Business Logic Tier: The business logic tier is where code translates user actions to application functionality. Amazon API Gateway builds a front door to the application's backend by creating REST or WebSocket APIs. API Gateway processes hundreds of thousands of concurrent API calls with traffic management, authorization and access control, monitoring, and API version management. API Gateway provides 1 million monthly API calls. AWS Lambda provides a serverless compute environment that integrates with API Gateway. Business logic is embedded into functions that run on AWS without the need to run and manage infrastructure. The Always Free Tier offers 1 million free requests and 400,000 GB-seconds of compute time per month usable for functions across both x86 and AWS Graviton processors. Lambda functions can be written in multiple languages including Python, Node.js, Java, Go, and .NET. API Gateway integrates with Amazon Cognito for JWT-based authorization, validating tokens on every request before forwarding to Lambda. Lambda execution roles use AWS IAM policies scoped with least privilege to access only the specific DynamoDB tables and S3 buckets they need.

Data Tier: The data tier is where application data is stored. Amazon DynamoDB is a serverless NoSQL database for storing data and tracking transactions. In the context of a three-tier architecture, DynamoDB stores and manages the application's data, providing reliable and secure data access to the business logic tier. The Always Free Tier offers 25 GB of free storage, with up to 200 million requests, 25 write capacity units (WCUs), and 25 read capacity units (RCUs) per month. DynamoDB supports on-demand capacity mode, which automatically adapts to application traffic patterns. DynamoDB Streams can be enabled to capture item-level changes for real-time processing. Point-in-time recovery (PITR) provides continuous backups for the last 35 days. DynamoDB data is encrypted at rest by default using AWS-owned keys, and optionally with customer-managed AWS KMS keys.

Operational Excellence and Monitoring: Amazon CloudWatch collects and tracks metrics, collects and monitors log files, and sets alarms across all three tiers. CloudWatch Logs aggregates Lambda execution logs, API Gateway access logs, and custom application metrics. CloudWatch Alarms can trigger notifications via Amazon SNS when thresholds are breached, such as elevated error rates or increased latency. AWS CloudTrail enables audit logging by recording all API calls made across the AWS account, providing a complete history of actions for security analysis and compliance. AWS X-Ray provides distributed tracing to track requests as they flow from CloudFront through API Gateway to Lambda and DynamoDB, enabling identification of performance bottlenecks and debugging of errors.

Security: AWS IAM manages fine-grained access control between services. Each Lambda function has a dedicated execution role with least-privilege permissions. API Gateway resource policies restrict access to the API. S3 bucket policies and CloudFront Origin Access Control (OAC) ensure that S3 content can only be accessed through CloudFront, not directly. All data flows through HTTPS with TLS 1.2 or higher. DynamoDB encryption at rest uses AWS KMS. VPC endpoints can be configured for private connectivity between Lambda and DynamoDB without traversing the public internet.

The end-to-end data flow is as follows: Users authenticate through Amazon Cognito and navigate to the website hosted on S3, delivered via CloudFront in the presentation tier. Authenticated users call REST APIs through API Gateway, which validates the Cognito JWT token and invokes Lambda functions at the business logic tier. Lambda functions execute business logic and perform CRUD operations against DynamoDB at the data tier. Responses flow back through API Gateway to the client. All interactions are logged in CloudWatch and CloudTrail for operational visibility and compliance.
